item.title: Beppu Onsen Festival — Guide
item.description: The Beppu Onsen Festival (Beppu Onsen Matsuri), held each year in early April, is the town’s biggest celebration, giving thanks to the gods and the earth for the endless bounty of hot springs that has made Beppu Japan’s greatest onsen town. Over several days the whole town comes alive with festivities: colourful parades with music, dance and floats through the streets, a lively hot-spring ‘mikoshi’ (portable shrine), and events across Beppu’s eight hot-spring districts.

item.title: Dogo Onsen Spring Festival — Guide
item.description: The Dogo Onsen Spring Festival (Dogo Onsen Matsuri) is the annual celebration of the historic hot-spring town of Dogo, held over several days in spring. Centred on the famous Dogo Onsen Honkan bathhouse and the surrounding arcade and streets, it fills the onsen quarter with traditional dances, music, costumed processions and events honouring the town’s long history and the gods of the hot spring. The atmospheric setting — the grand old wooden bathhouse, the shopping arcade and the hot-spring town in the fresh green of spring — makes it a charming, less overwhelming festival than the great summer events, and a lovely time to combine a soak at Dogo Onsen with a taste of local celebration in Matsuyama.

item.title: Ashikaga Flower Park: A 150-Year-Old Giant Wisteria Tree — Guide
item.description: Ashikaga Flower Park is home to a single great wisteria tree over 150 years old, its sprawling branches trained across a vast trellis covering roughly 1,000 square metres, blooming each late April into May into a cascading canopy of purple, pink and white blossoms that CNN once ranked among the world’s ‘dream destinations.’ Beyond the wisteria season, the park hosts seasonal displays year-round, including a large-scale winter illumination that transforms the flower beds into a light show after dark.

item.title: Takada Castle Ruins: 4,000 Cherry Trees & Japan's Great Night Blossoms — Guide
item.description: Takada Castle, once home to a feudal lord and later a military garrison, survives today primarily as a moated park rather than a standing keep, but its roughly 4,000 cherry trees have earned it a place among Japan’s three great night cherry blossom viewing spots. Each spring, the annual Takada Cherry Blossom Festival illuminates the trees and their reflections in the surrounding moat, drawing large crowds for an evening spectacle that ranks among the most photographed cherry blossom scenes in the country.

item.title: Hitsujiyama Park Shibazakura: A Carpet of Pink Moss Phlox — Guide
item.description: Hitsujiyama Park in Chichibu is home to one of Japan’s most spectacular shibazakura (moss phlox) displays, where roughly 400,000 plants bloom across nine varieties into a vivid patchwork of pink, white and purple each April and May. The flower fields are arranged in undulating patterns across a hillside with Mount Buko rising in the background, and the annual Shibazakura Festival held during peak bloom draws large crowds with food stalls and local produce alongside the floral spectacle.
